title: The Miller and His Wife
logline: A miller dreams of gold buried on his donkey s path and tells his wife; she betrays the secret to a neighbour who kills her for the whole hoard, and at dawn the miller kills the donkey that was only trying to warn him.
moral: A secret told to the wrong person costs everything, and anger punishes the innocent: the donkey was afraid, not stubborn.
tone: A dark fable told with restraint: warm and gently comic for the first third, then night, greed and silence. Violence is shown only as shadows, a lamp going out and stillness.

beats.summary: The mill, the ring and the donkey that walks it.
He loves her; she leans toward the neighbour, who keeps away.
The dream: gold under one spot of the ring.
He tells his wife and asks for secrecy.
She runs straight to the neighbour.
Her plan to share and marry; his plan to take it all.
He kills her (lamp out) and flees with the gold, leaving the pit open.
The donkey stops at the pit; the miller cannot see why.
In his rage he kills the donkey.
Daylight shows him wife, donkey and treasure all lost.
The neighbour is gone with the money.

sets.description: New shared set (see new_assets): cutaway donkey mill interior, 1000 x 1230, floor line y 900. Used in S1, S7 to S11, S13 to S19, S21 with options u (window sky), dark 0..1, door 0..1, turn (stone angle), pit {open 0..1}, mound 0..1, layer 'back' / 'front'.

The lane between the houses: villageYard with the default cottage at the right edge as the NEIGHBOUR S house (door anchor about x 800, measure on the set), tree false or far left, u 0.25 in S2, u 0.4 to 0.72 in S5 with winLit.
countryRoad w 2400, u 0.03 (sunrise), default places; one tree used as a foreground wipe with the front pass.

props.description: Library heart(ctx, x, y, r): r 30 to 48. Miller s heart (S2), wife s smaller heart (S2, S5).

Planned coinPile (mound of n 0..40 coins, about 220 wide x 90 high at n 40, with a ghost dashed outline option) and a single coin (yellow disc r 12, black outline, inner ring) that can arc, roll and glint.
Planned shovel: wooden shaft 150 long x 8, grey iron blade 40 x 52 with a rounded tip, drawn about a grip point with rot.
packLoad(ctx, ['sack'], x, y, s) for the coin sack; in the tug it is stretched by scaling x up to 1.25; a yellow coin mark drawn on it by the scene.
Scene drawn: the wife s yellow headscarf as a loose cloth (a 70 x 40 quad with two folds, yellow with red dots, black outline) that drifts down and lies by the pit.
Small knife: white blade 60 x 14 with a pointed tip, brown handle 30 x 12, black outline, optional 4 point glint star. Never shown touching the donkey.
The Library lamp drawing used as a floor lamp (hangingLamp without its chain, or the chain length 0) with a yellow halftone disc r 170; it rocks with swing() and goes out at 95.76.

subtitles.ar: كان طحان يعيش مع زوجته ويعمل كل يوم في طاحونة يديرها حمار.|أحب الرجل زوجته كثيرًا، لكنها لم تبادله الحب؛|فقد كانت تميل إلى جار لهما، بينما كان الجار يبتعد عنها.
subtitles.en: A miller lived with his wife and worked each day at a mill turned by a donkey.|He loved her,|but she was drawn to a neighbor who kept his distance.

subtitles.ar: رأى الطحان في منامه شخصًا يقول له:|احفر في مكان معين من طريق الحمار حول الطاحونة، فهناك مال مدفون.|استيقظ فرحًا، وأخبر زوجته بالحلم، وطلب منها أن تحفظ السر.
subtitles.en: In a dream someone told the miller|to dig at a particular place along the donkey’s circular path, where money lay buried.|He told his wife and urged secrecy.

subtitles.ar: لم تحفظ الزوجة السر، بل أسرعت إلى الجار الذي كانت تحبه.|اتفقا على الحفر ليلًا، وحين نام الطحان|دخلا الطاحونة وحفرا في الموضع المذكور، فظهرت أمامهما كنوز من النقود.
subtitles.en: Instead, the wife told the neighbor she loved.|They agreed to dig at night and, while the miller slept,|uncovered a hoard of coins in the mill.

subtitles.ar: قالت الزوجة: نقسم المال نصفين،|ثم تترك زوجتك وأتخلص أنا من زوجي، فنتزوج ونجمع المال.|لكن الجار أراد أن يأخذ الكنز كله،|وخاف أن تهرب بنصيبها إلى رجل آخر.
subtitles.en: She suggested splitting the treasure,|leaving their spouses, marrying, and combining their shares.|But the neighbor wanted all the money|and feared she would leave him.

subtitles.ar: رفضت المرأة أن تسلمه حصتها، فاشتد الخلاف بينهما.|غلب الطمع على الجار فقتلها، وألقى جسدها في الحفرة الفارغة.|أخذ النقود وهرب، ولم يسعفه الوقت ليردم الحفرة قبل الفجر.
subtitles.en: She refused to surrender her share.|Driven by greed, the neighbor killed her, threw her body into the empty pit,|took the coins, and fled before dawn.

subtitles.ar: استيقظ الطحان فلم يجد زوجته،|ثم ذهب إلى الطاحونة وربط الحمار ليدور كعادته.|تقدم الحيوان قليلًا ثم توقف خائفًا؛ فقد رأى الجسد في الحفرة،|أما صاحبه فلم يفهم سبب توقفه.
subtitles.en: The miller woke to find his wife missing.|At the mill he harnessed the donkey,|which stopped in fright at the body in the pit.|The miller did not understand.

subtitles.ar: صرخ الرجل في الحمار وضربه، لكنه رفض الحركة.|ازداد غضب الطحان، فأخذ سكينًا وطعنه مرارًا حتى مات.|لم يكن يعرف أن الحيوان كان يخاف مما رآه، لا يعاند صاحبه.
subtitles.en: He shouted and beat the donkey, but it would not move.|Angry, he repeatedly stabbed it until it died,|unaware that it had been terrified rather than stubborn.

subtitles.ar: عندما طلع النهار رأى الطحان زوجته ميتة في الحفرة،|وحماره ميتًا بجانبها، والكنز قد اختفى.|بقي حزينًا على خسائره كلها، بينما كان الجار قد مضى بالمال، كما تروي الحكاية.
subtitles.en: At daylight the miller found his wife dead in the pit,|his donkey dead beside it, and the treasure gone.|The neighbor had escaped with the money.

new_assets.name: millHouse
new_assets.description: Cutaway donkey mill for any miller, oil press or water wheel story. World 1000 x 1230, floor line y 900 (floor fills to 1230, earth brown with dark dot shading). Walls x 60..940, roof beam y 250..280, ochre back wall with red dot shading. Door in the left wall (x 60..190, top y 560). Window in the back wall x 760..880, y 380..500 showing skyCycle(u). Millstone at centre: bed stone 230 wide x 80 high (x 385..615, y 820..900), runner stone 190 x 56 on top (y 764..820) with 6 radial stripes that slide with `turn`, a vertical post 16 wide from the runner to the roof beam, a wooden hopper 110 x 90 hung at (430, 640) and a flour tray at the left foot. Sweep beam: a 12 thick pole from the post at (500, 770) to the donkey collar. Ring: an ellipse worn into the floor, centre (500, 905), rx 320, ry 55 (back of the ring y 850, front y 960), drawn as a lighter band 26 wide with hoof dots. Sacks and a hopper table at far left (x 90..230). Pit anchor at ring angle about 62 degrees toward the front right: an ellipse 210 x 64 centred (650, 962), navy inside with blue dots, with a 14 unit lip; mound of earth 160 wide x 66 high at (800, 950).
new_assets.implementation: One function millHouse(ctx, o) in Library/sets returning anchors {floor, door, window, stone, post, ring {cx, cy, rx, ry}, pit {x, y, w, h, rim}, mound, hopper}. Static parts baked with bake(); live parts: door (townDoor), window (skyCycle clipped), runner stripes (turn), pit (open 0..1 scales the ellipse and its depth shade), mound (0..1 height), dark 0..1 (navy overlay with a clear disc at o.lampAt), light shaft (yellow halftone quad from the window, o.shaft 0..1 with its foot x keyed). Two passes: layer 'back' (walls, back half of the ring, stone), cast, then layer 'front' (pit lip and mound front edge) so a figure lowered into the pit is clipped by the rim. Helper millRing(theta) returns {x, y, dir, s, behind} on the ellipse: x = cx + rx cos(theta), y = cy + ry sin(theta), s = 0.9 + 0.1 * (sin + 1) / 2, behind = sin < 0 (draw before the stone), dir from the travel direction; leg phase from walk(distFn, t, {stride: GAIT.donkey * s}) where distFn = 0.72 * rx * theta(t).

owner_questions: The wife s killing (95.76) is not shown: the neighbour s wall shadow raises the shovel, the lamp goes out, and only her scarf falls. Default: keep it off screen like this.

Her body is shown only as a still, closed eyed figure in deep shadow inside the pit (97.5 to 99.8, an 0.8 s insert at 124.96, and at 157.9), with no wound or blood. Default: show it this softly; the alternative is to show only the scarf and a hand.
The donkey s stabbing (142.32 to 144.2) is told by wall shadows and three white flashes, the knife never touches it on screen, then it lies still with closed eyes. Default: shadows only.
The beating (134.5, 135.4) is shown directly as two comic stick blows with WHACK! lettering. Default: keep two blows.

Added staging not in the script: hearts for the love triangle, the neighbour sweeping his step, the miller turning to his hopper so that he cannot see the pit, one coin left behind, and the final return to the mill after the neighbour s road. Default: keep them.

English lettering added: THE MILLER, THE MILL, THE DONKEY, THE NEIGHBOR, EVERY DAY, DIG!, SHH!, CLANK!, HALF, ALL MINE!, NO!, HER SHARE, MOVE!, WHACK!, HEE HAW!, AFRAID, NOT STUBBORN, GONE, Z Z Z, ONE NIGHT... Default: keep; AFRAID, NOT STUBBORN states the moral on screen.

SCRIPT: P8 English omits two Arabic phrases (he remained grieving over all his losses; as the tale tells) and P3 English omits that she hurried to the neighbour and that they dug at the stated spot. Both languages are kept verbatim; default: no change.
implementation_notes: Cue every action to timeline.json word starts (w(p, n) in the template); the times in this plan are those starts.

Set LIFE.t = t each frame so everyone blinks; suppress blinks (noBlink) on the cold stare 71.84 to 73.7, the standoff 92.34 to 93.5, the miller 139.66 to 141.5 and the donkey s wide eye 122.88 to 125.8.

Draw order in millHouse: layer back, donkey if millRing behind, stone and beam, cast and donkey in front, pit contents (clipped to the pit ellipse), layer front (lip and mound), darkness overlay, lamp disc, light shaft, lettering, finish last.

The donkey s ring walk: key theta(t) only; position, facing, scale and draw order come from millRing(theta); legs from walk() on the arc distance so the hooves never slide. In S13 theta goes from the front left (about 150 degrees) to about 105 degrees and stops there, two strides short of the pit at 62 degrees.

The miller must never face the pit between 113.36 and 155.9: he works at the far left, stands behind the donkey s rump, and the right half of the mill stays at dark 0.55 until the light shaft at 154.34.
Darkness: dark 0.85 on entry (56.32) with the lamp disc following the lamp; 0.5 while they dig and talk; 1.0 from 95.76 (2 frames) to 97.46; 0.6 to 107; 0.55 from 113.36; 0.4 at 149.6; 0 by 155.5.

Violence rules: no blood anywhere, no contact frames for the shovel or the knife, flashes are 2 frames of paper white inside the panel only. The pit figure is the wife in lie 1, lid 1, under a navy overlay.

Sound: 8 quiet effects only, all in listed pauses (8.2 tick, 17.7 pop, 21.7 whoosh, 43.3 pop, 64.75 chime, 108.65 thud, 113.0 pop) plus one low chime at 175.0 after the last word. The killing, the beating and the stabbing have no effects: the narration has no pauses there and silence is stronger.
Use twoShot() for S4, S8, S10, S14 and S15; panel-only shake for the tug and the blows; the one transition card is ONE NIGHT... centred on 21.7 with the set change hidden at its midpoint.
Subtitles: 24 chunks as marked in the subtitles array (verbatim, checked by plancheck). Lettering never covers a face and stays inside the picture panel.
Costume check on first stills: the miller (beanSeller, brown) and the neighbour (villager, green) must be told apart at phone size; if not, give the neighbour pal {robe: blue}.
warnings: Dark material (a murder and the killing of an animal). The plan keeps both off screen; see owner_questions 1 to 4 before animating.

millHouse is a large new set and the film depends on it (14 of 21 scenes). Build and approve it with stills first: ring perspective, donkey passing behind the stone, pit and mound, darkness and light shaft.
hunterShadow, coinEyes, flush, iconBalloon, goldGlow, coinPile, shovel and sneak are planned by other stories but not in Library yet; if they exist by then, use the Library versions.

The person figure is front facing only: lowering the body (97.46) is staged with the neighbour s back implied by hiding his face behind a raised shoulder and the mound; check that it reads, otherwise stage it wholly behind the mound.
Narration is dense from 65 s to 107 s and 118 s to 152 s (no pauses of 0.6 s): no sound effects are planned there.
The Library person has no profile, so the stick blow and the pushing at 130.04 rely on arm angles and body tip; test these poses on a contact sheet.
